title: The Paperwork Pals
markdown:
The memo landed with a soft thump. Directive 74-B: Streamlining Inter-Departmental Synergy. Its thickness promised hours of linguistic gymnastics.

Ester Novak, the department translator, felt the familiar prickle. The office hummed, a low drone of hushed anxieties. She adjusted her spectacles and fixed her gaze on the first paragraph, a dense thicket of jargon.

Pavel Zoric, the committee optimist, bounced into her cubicle. "Ester, my dear. Have you seen the new directive? Simply marvelous. A real step forward in efficiency." He gestured vaguely, as if the memo radiated progress.

"Pavel," she said, voice flat, "this synergy directive appears to create three new sub-committees and a Synergy Oversight Council. And that is just page one." She tapped a convoluted sentence.

Pavel clapped, oblivious. "Exactly. More collaboration. Think of the paperwork." His enthusiasm bloomed stubbornly in the arid desert of officialdom.

Ester sighed. "The first task is to translate this directive into the Unified Lexicon of Procedural Clarity. According to Appendix C, that requires consultation with the newly formed Advisory Board for Terminological Harmonization." The name itself was a small masterpiece of redundancy.

"Splendid." Pavel was already scheduling appointments in his head. "I will put in a request for their immediate formation. And perhaps a sub-committee to oversee the formation of the formation sub-committee?" He winked, a flicker of self-aware humor.

Across the hall, an Office of Office Formation blinked into existence. Its job: approving new offices. Its paperwork: already a Jenga tower of officialdom, threatening to collapse.

The department became a whirlwind of paper. Ester drowned in translation requests. Pavel attended the Synergy Oversight Council. They debated optimal font size for memos for three hours. He reported back, beaming. "Times New Roman, size 12. A monumental decision for inter-departmental clarity."

Ester just nodded, scanning a fresh stack. "The Advisory Board for Terminological Harmonization has requested a translator for their Lexicon-In-Progress project. They also propose a Sub-Committee for Lexicon-Adjacent Terminology. Apparently synergy has several adjacent connotations needing precise definition."

A booming voice echoed. The Director, his suits always seeming borrowed, strode in, a thicker memo clutched like a scepter. "Comrades. I have reviewed Directive 74-B. We need a more robust framework for procedural streamlining. Therefore I announce the establishment of the Grand Directorate of Departmental Harmonization and Efficiency."

Pavel’s smile widened. "Another step forward."

Ester’s shoulders slumped. "And what does this Directorate do, Pavel? Beyond adding another layer to the labyrinth?"

"It oversees all streamlining procedures. And its first directive," he squinted, a flicker of uncertainty vanishing, "is to appoint a Senior Translator for streamlining translations, and a Chief Optimist to champion efficiency initiatives."

They looked at each other. The silence stretched, broken only by the whirring of a new duplicating machine. A shared understanding. A silent acknowledgment of the cosmic joke.

Ester was at her desk, the Unified Lexicon of Procedural Clarity open. Pavel sat beside her, tapping his pen on a blank form. The new memo lay between them, a testament to the enduring power of paper.

She picked up her pen, a ghost of a smile. "Well, Pavel. At least we have each other to translate this particular brand of progress. It is almost comforting, in a profoundly absurd way."

Pavel nodded, eyes shining. "Indeed, Ester. A partnership forged in administrative chaos. Now, about this Lexicon-Adjacent Terminology subcommittee. I believe it requires a subcommittee for sub-subcommittee terminology, do you not think?"

The paper system, vast and unyielding, continued to churn. They, the weary but resilient cogs, bound by shared experience and dry wit, began their work anew, finding a quiet solace in the absurdity, and in each other.
characters: Ester Novak (department translator), Pavel Zoric (committee optimist)
